newsitem.title: USA: Henkel raises bid for Loctite - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Henkel raises bid for Loctite - WSJ.

text.p: Germany's Henkel KGaA has embarked on a hostile tender offer for the 65 percent of Loctite Corp shares that it does not already own, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday.
The newspaper said Henkel had risen its offering price to $57.75 a share from $56 a share or $1.19 billion.
The new price would value the company at 11.2 times the estimates for its 1997 cash flow, it added.
Loctite had set up a special committee last week to review Henkel's initial acquisition proposal of $56 a share.
Henkel had said that it wanted to enter into productive talks that would lead to a friendly takeover agreement. If such talks failed to progress, it could start a public tender, it said.
One of the definitions of a permitted offer is a tender offer that remains open for 60 days and wins more than 50 percent of the shares, which would in effect put Loctite up for auction.
